details: Bitcoin experienced a significant price drop, reaching multi-month lows around $62,000, influenced by substantial outflows from US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs). Concerns over potential interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve and a perceived shift of investor capital towards Artificial Intelligence (AI) stocks have contributed to a broader risk-off sentiment in the cryptocurrency market. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index currently reflects "extreme fear" among investors.
title: Bitcoin Falls to Multi-Month Low Amid ETF Outflows & Rate Hike Fears

details: European Central Bank (ECB) Deputy Governor Boris Vujčić indicated that market expectations for additional interest rate hikes in 2027 are "not unreasonable." He stressed that future rate decisions would depend on evolving inflation trends. Current on-chain analysis suggests investors anticipate two 25-basis-point increases after December. Additionally, the ECB highlighted heightened financial stability risks stemming from geopolitical tensions, energy price shocks, and rising public debt within the euro area.
title: ECB Deputy Signals Further Rate Hikes Possible in 2027

details: The Nasdaq Composite has seen a notable decline, primarily driven by a sell-off in semiconductor stocks, particularly Nvidia, following its CEO's resignation and ahead of its upcoming earnings report. This increased volatility in the tech sector, coupled with the narrative of AI companies attracting investor interest, has contributed to a broader risk-off mood that is negatively impacting cryptocurrency prices.
title: Tech Sell-off Led by Nvidia Weighs on Crypto Markets

details: The total supply of tokenized equities has reached an unprecedented $3.8 billion, representing a remarkable 590% growth over the past year. This surge is attributed to increasing institutional interest and forthcoming retail investor access in the U.S. due to recent regulatory approvals. This development highlights a significant "bull market in crypto" for real-world asset tokenization, indicating a growing integration of traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.
title: Tokenized Equities Hit Record High of $3.8 Billion

details: South Africa's National Treasury and Reserve Bank are revising their regulations for cross-border cryptocurrency transactions. Following extensive public feedback, the updated framework will move away from requiring pre-approvals for such transactions, instead focusing on verifying their legitimacy and ensuring tax compliance. This shift aims to facilitate the legitimate movement of digital assets while maintaining necessary oversight.
title: South Africa Shifts Crypto Rules: From Pre-Approval to Verification
